extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO (respondents in OED disciplinary matters)
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving a USPTO disciplinary proceeding by settlement; it states jurisdiction, stipulated facts, legal conclusion, mitigating considerations, agreed sanctions, probation conditions, and procedural remedies for noncompliance. Useful as the governing checklist of requirements and procedures applicable to a disciplined USPTO-registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes and regulations provide the legal basis for OED to enter into a settlement Agreement and for the USPTO Director to approve and issue the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for USPTO rule violation (public discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) (being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public discipline by a state authority (e.g., Minnesota Supreme Court order) constitutes a violation of this USPTO rule and is sufficient to support discipline at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law professional misconduct allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations in the Minnesota petition included violating Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct 1.15(a), 8.1(a), 8.1(b), and 8.4(c), and Rule 25 of the Minnesota Rules on Lawyers Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These state rules were the predicate for the state disciplinary action (fabrication/backdating of fee agreement; multiple knowingly false statements; improper use of trust account; allowing non-lawyer signatory; failing to cooperate with investigation). The Final Order treats those findings as relevant to USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misconduct alleged: making multiple knowingly false statements to the OLPR Director; fabricating and backdating a fee agreement; allowing respondent's wife to use his trust account for personal transactions; allowing a non-lawyer to be the sole signatory on his trust account; failing to cooperate with an investigation by the OLPR Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual misconduct types are examples of behavior that can result in public discipline and trigger USPTO professional-conduct violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in reaching settlement (mitigating factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED considered that respondent (1) accepted responsibility for his actions; (2) expressed contrition and understands the seriousness of his actions and how they violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; (3) had not been previously publicly disciplined in more than 27 years of practice; and (4) provided full and fair disclosures to OED during the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of responsibility, contrition, lack of prior public discipline, and full/cooperative disclosure are mitigating factors that can affect the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed suspension sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended nunc pro tunc for a period of 30 days from May 13, 2020, until June 12, 2020, from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the suspension is nunc pro tunc, it is deemed to have been served and the respondent is reinstated to practice before the Office in matters in which he is otherwise eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a two-year probationary period commencing nunc pro tunc on June 13, 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The probation is a time-limited period during which specified conditions apply; violations during probation can trigger further sanctions, including an additional one-year suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLE requirement as condition of probation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of probation respondent shall (i) complete at least eight (8) hours of continuing legal education (CLE) courses in which the primary subject is general legal ethics, trust accounting for lawyers, and/or a lawyer's duty of candor, (ii) file an affidavit with the OED Director attesting to completion, and (iii) provide documentation corroborating the affidavit, within one year of the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This CLE requirement is mandatory during probation; compliance must be evidenced by affidavit plus corroborating documentation and is time-limited (one year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause (OSC) initiation and notice procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), and grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OSC is the formal procedural first step for alleged probation noncompliance; mailing to the last address of record and a 15-day response period are procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation to immediate suspension after OSC
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day period the OED Director remains of the opinion respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director (i) the OSC, (ii) respondent's response, if any, and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the opinion, and request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend respondent from practice before the USPTO for an additional one year, not on nunc pro tunc basis, for the violation set forth in the Joint Legal Conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the evidentiary and decision pathway for imposing an additional non-nunc pro tunc suspension based on probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stay of suspension pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends respondent pursuant to paragraph 'e' and respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review or appeal does not stay an imposed suspension; the suspension remains in effect during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's authority to seek further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 through 11.57 for any misconduct engaged in by respondent prior to, during, or after his probationary period, including that which formed the basis for an OSC or which led to the imposition of a suspension pursuant to paragraph 'e'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order does not limit future disciplinary actions; prior proceedings may be considered as aggravating factors in subsequent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief from certain suspension-related obligations (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the suspension is deemed to have already been served, respondent shall not be required to: (1) submit an affidavit of compliance under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2); (2) file a notice of withdrawal in any pending application under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(i); (3) deliver client documents under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(iv); (4) relinquish client funds for practice before the Office under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(v); (5) remove any telephone, legal or other directory advertisement, statement, or representation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(vi); and (6) change any existing advertising regarding availability under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(4); (7) change any sign or stationery per 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated obligations normally associated with suspension are explicitly waived because the suspension is retroactively treated as served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that he has provided notice of his suspension to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies to which he is admitted to practice as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references the requirement to notify jurisdictions upon suspension; here respondent represents compliance with that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client arrangements and conflict avoidance during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that he does not have clients having immediate or prospective business before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii) and has made appropriate arrangements for legal services to be rendered on behalf of his clients during his period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners under suspension must avoid pending matters before the Office and make arrangements to protect client interests; this representation is treated as a fact in the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-granting of limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Because respondent's suspension is deemed to have already been served, respondent shall not be granted limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deemed-served suspension precludes granting limited recognition under the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's publicly accessible electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted publicly; the Official Gazette notice must summarize the suspension, probation, CLE requirement, applicable rule violated, facts of the state proceeding, and the OED Director's considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning respondent, and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent (i) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline, and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf, and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record of this case is available to the Office and may be used in aggravation or rebuttal in future matters; the Final Order explicitly preserves that usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives the opportunity: (i) to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.56 or 11.57, (ii) to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and (iii) otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By entering the settlement Agreement respondent gives up specified administrative and appellate rights to challenge the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties bear their own costs in complying with the terms of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No party is awarded costs to be paid by the other in complying with the Order.
